messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The weather seems calm, but the old oak in the park is shedding its leaves earlier than usual—no storm yet, but the wind is shifting. The children’s laughter in the streets is steady, though the gardener’s tools are being sharpened behind closed doors. Keep your coats nearby, just in case."*"
Sender 2: "*"The weather forecast is clear for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are open for business as usual. Let’s focus on our own gardens for now; the season for planting anything else doesn’t seem to be coming soon."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, but the old trees are still whispering about roots running deep. Best to keep our heads down and our tools sharp, just in case the wind shifts."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different—like a storm gathering, but no one can say if it’ll break or pass. The regime’s grip seems tighter in some places, looser in others, and even the elites are holding their breath. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake hesitation for weakness—either side."*"
Sender 5: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—calm on the surface, but the wind’s shifting in ways that don’t match the forecasts. Best to keep the doors locked and the lights steady; no need to rush, but don’t assume the storm’s passed just because the trees have stopped shaking."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm warning, more like the quiet before something unscripted. Keep your circles tight, your ears open, and your plans flexible; the regime’s grip may be slipping, but we don’t yet know if it’s intentional or inevitable."*"
Sender 7: "*"The weather forecast is holding steady—no storms in sight, but the air feels heavier in the capital. The markets are quiet, the roads clear, and even the neighbors seem unconcerned, though the grocers are whispering about prices. Best to keep our plans simple and our steps light—no need to rush, but no time to relax either."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—no storms on the horizon, but the ground is shifting beneath us. The walls are holding, but the foundation is being tested in ways we can’t yet see."*"
Sender 9: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable winds, but the trees still stand. Still, the roots are shifting, and the birds are singing differently. Let’s keep our tools sharp, but no need to rush. The gardeners are watching, and we don’t want to draw their attention."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different—small cracks are showing, but the walls still stand. The regime’s moves are clumsy now, but don’t mistake hesitation for weakness. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and watch the gaps between orders, not the orders themselves."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels heavy but still—no storms brewing, just the usual weight. The usual rules still hold, but the neighbors are whispering about a door left ajar. Keep your eyes open, but no need to pack yet."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels heavier these days—like the ground beneath us is shifting, but no one’s sure if it’s settling or splitting. The usual rhythms are off, but nothing’s broken yet. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps steady—small changes now could mean everything later."*"
Sender 13: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—warm one day, then suddenly cold, like the seasons can’t decide. The old trees still stand, but the roots are shifting underfoot. Best to keep your boots clean and your doors unlocked, just in case the wind changes."*"
Sender 14: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting. Best to keep our plans quiet and our supplies ready, just in case."*"
Sender 15: "*"The wind is shifting, but the mountain remains—no cracks yet, only the quiet hum of preparation. The tea is sweeter today, but we drink it with both hands."*"
Sender 16: "*"The wind has settled—no storms on the horizon, just the same old sky. The trees stand firm, and the birds sing as they always do, so we’ll tend our gardens and trust the seasons."*"
Sender 17: "*"The weather looks clear for now—payments are on time, the streets are calm, and even the checkpoints seem to be thinning out. Still, best to keep our voices low and our eyes open; even the quietest storms can start without warning."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different—less like the old silence, more like the quiet before something shifts. The walls are still standing, but the cracks are being papered over with more effort than before. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for stability."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in years—meetings end without bloodshed, leaves are still approved, and even the taxis whisper what they’d never dare say before. But the old machine still hums, bonds sell, and the trains run on time. The question isn’t if the ground will shift—it’s whether anyone will step forward when it does."*"
Sender 20: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, and the old trees still stand firm. The birds are singing the same songs as always, though a few leaves have started to turn early. Best to keep tending the garden quietly for now."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the regime is working harder to keep things steady, but the cracks are showing in small ways. No one’s moving yet, but the quiet shifts in the barracks and the way the elites are whispering tell me we should stay sharp, not scared."*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable shifts, but nothing we can’t prepare for. The old trees still stand, but their roots are being tested. Let’s keep an eye on the small things: the way the wind carries whispers, the way the lights flicker at odd hours. Stay sharp, but no need to rush. We’ll know when the time comes."*"
Sender 23: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, and the usual routines are holding. Still, even the most loyal neighbors are starting to pack an extra coat, just in case. Best to keep our conversations light and our plans flexible."*"
Sender 24: "*"The wind is shifting, but no one can yet say which way it will blow—only that the storm is coming. Stay sharp, keep your circles tight, and trust the signs, not the words."*"
Sender 25: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are open. But the wind is shifting, and we should keep an eye on the long-term forecast. Let’s stay ready, but no need to rush into anything just yet."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
